title: Legacy UOM Conversion Gap in Migrated Purchase History
scenario_text:
Ironforge Manufacturing is 14 months into its SAP S/4HANA migration from SAP ECC. The Monterrey (Mexico) plant still runs ECC 6.0 and is scheduled for cutover in Q3 2026. During a supplier performance review, a discrepancy surfaces in vendor pricing for titanium fastener stock (material 4400-TF-0882 in S/4HANA).

**SAP S/4HANA — Purchase Order History (migrated records)**
Material: 4400-TF-0882 | Vendor: Precision Alloys Ltd (Vendor #300442)
PO 450012881 (migrated from legacy): Qty 500 EA @ $14.20/EA = $7,100.00
PO 450012997 (migrated from legacy): Qty 200 EA @ $14.20/EA = $2,840.00
PO 450018330 (new, post-migration): Qty 1,000 EA @ $1.42/EA = $1,420.00

**SharePoint — /migration/mapping-tables/UOM-conversion-log.xlsx (last modified: Nov 2024)**
Row 2,841: Material 4400-TF-0882 | Legacy UOM: HUN (per hundred) | Target UOM: EA (each)
Conversion factor: 0.01 | Applied to: Material master, BOM, routing
Note column: "Historical PO price migration — FLAG: conversion NOT applied to closed POs per cutover decision doc v2.3. Only open POs at cutover converted."

**Microsoft Teams — #erp-migration-war-room (Feb 12, 2025, 3:47 PM)**
@raj.chowdhury: Heads up — closed PO pricing in the migrated history is going to look 100x inflated vs. new POs for any material that was HUN in legacy. We made the call not to restate historical pricing during cutover. It's documented in the cutover decision log.
@maria.santos: Got it. Should we flag these for procurement reporting?
@raj.chowdhury: Already raised it in the data steward meeting. Karen said she'd add a note to the reporting wiki.
[3 emoji reactions: thumbs-up from maria.santos, eyes from dave.kowalski, no reaction from karen.mills]

**SAP ECC (Mexico plant, still live) — Vendor Master**
Vendor: Precision Alloys de Mexico SA de CV (Vendor #VM-8821)
Purchasing org: 1200 (Monterrey)
Payment terms: Net 45
Note: "Same entity as HQ vendor 300442 — see cross-reference in Oracle decomm mapping"

**Oracle Procurement (decommissioned Dec 2023) — Archived Extract on SharePoint**
/migration/oracle-archive/vendor-xref.csv
Row: Oracle Vendor ID OV-4410 | SAP ECC Vendor VM-8821 | SAP S/4 Vendor 300442 | Entity: "Precision Alloys Group (all subsidiaries)"
Note: "Consolidated from 3 Oracle vendor IDs (OV-4410, OV-4411, OV-4415) during ECC implementation 2017"
question: A procurement analyst is reviewing total spend with Precision Alloys for contract renegotiation. They pull all PO history from S/4HANA for vendor 300442 and calculate an average unit price of $9.94/EA across 1,700 units. What is the correct interpretation and what action should they take?

contributor.name: Raj Chowdhury
contributor.title: ERP Migration & Data Governance Lead
contributor.domain_expertise: Data migration, legacy system decommissioning, master data reconciliation, cutover planning

choices: The migrated historical POs reflect a per-hundred UOM that was not restated during cutover; the true legacy price was $0.142/EA, making the current $1.42/EA actually a price increase — and the full spend picture requires cross-referencing vendor VM-8821 at the Mexico plant plus the three consolidated Oracle vendor IDs
Only post-migration POs should be used for negotiation since historical data is unreliable; vendor 300442 is the only relevant entity and the $1.42/EA rate represents the current market price
The average price is correct; the vendor has been charging inconsistent prices and procurement should flag this in the negotiation as evidence of price erosion opportunity

The pricing discrepancy indicates a data quality defect in the migration; the historical POs should be corrected in S/4HANA before any analysis, and the Mexico plant data is irrelevant since it is a different legal entity
